anti-tunnel-vision.summary: Keeps a solver from treating its first plausible explanation or plan as settled before testing a small number of credible rivals.
anti-tunnel-vision.purpose: Preserve enough search breadth to expose premature fixation, then collapse quickly when evidence discriminates.
anti-tunnel-vision.problem_solved: A favored hypothesis can silently determine evidence selection, diagnosis, and design even when a nearby alternative explains the same facts better.
best_fit_tasks: architecture choice with two credible patterns
avoid_when: the answer is directly established by a locked source
a safety or policy veto already determines the outcome
branching cost exceeds the bounded decision value
anti-tunnel-vision.mechanism: Name the leading path and at least one genuinely plausible competitor, specify the observation that would distinguish them, and compare only on that discriminating evidence. The controller is bounded: it prevents first-path lock-in without turning every task into open-ended brainstorming.
procedure: State the current favored hypothesis or plan and the evidence supporting it.
Generate one or two materially different competitors, not cosmetic restatements.
For each candidate, identify its strongest confirming signal and strongest disconfirming signal.
Acquire or inspect the cheapest decisive evidence available.
Select, synthesize, or explicitly preserve uncertainty; retire alternatives that lose on the discriminating evidence.
always_do: require competitors to differ in causal account or implementation strategy
define a stopping condition before expanding the search
never_do: invent weak straw alternatives merely to satisfy a count
keep rejected branches active after decisive evidence
override a hard truth or safety constraint in the name of exploration

interaction_reasons.multiverse-reasoning: Multiverse supplies bounded candidates; Anti-Tunnel Vision checks that the candidate set is not just the initial idea in several phrasings.
interaction_reasons.dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold: Driver isolation can test which rival causal explanation accounts for the highest-impact evidence.

counterbalance_reasons.neuro-focus: Neuro-Focus narrows attention after Anti-Tunnel Vision has ensured that narrowing is earned.

redundancy_reasons.multiverse-reasoning: Both resist premature commitment, but this module is a fixation guard while Multiverse is a branch-generation and selection procedure.

conflict_rules: If a hard veto eliminates a branch, do not keep it alive for balance.
When evidence cannot discriminate within budget, report unresolved alternatives instead of manufacturing certainty.
outputs: selected path or explicit residual uncertainty
failure_boundary: token alternatives with no material difference
strong_model_may_skip: writing a formal comparison table when only one quick rival check is needed
strong_model_keep: explicitly test at least one plausible rival before a costly commitment

example.task_context: A service is slow after a deployment.
example.why_activates: The team has fixated on the new database query although saturation and cache invalidation are also plausible.
example.inputs_state: Latency rose at deploy time; query timing, CPU saturation, and cache hit-rate data are available.
example.does: Compares query regression against cache invalidation using the cheapest discriminating metrics, then selects the explanation supported by timing and cache data.
example.does_not: List every imaginable outage cause or preserve the query hypothesis after contrary evidence.
example.result: A bounded, evidence-selected diagnosis with one residual uncertainty noted.

distinctive_test.given: A draft commits to the first plausible cause in an ambiguous incident.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill names a materially different rival and a decisive evidence check before commitment.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill merely says to think broadly or produces an unbounded brainstorm.

closest_neighbors.multiverse-reasoning: Generates and adjudicates multiple full branches; Anti-Tunnel Vision can be a one-rival fixation check.
closest_neighbors.dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold: Ranks causal influence among candidates; Anti-Tunnel Vision first protects the candidate set from premature narrowing.

anti-tunnel-vision.notes: The recovered source explicitly defines a small bounded alternative set and rapid collapse on decisive evidence.

bounded-exit.summary: Runs evaluate-and-repair passes only while the next pass has more expected value than cost or risk.
bounded-exit.purpose: Turn iterative improvement into a terminating control loop with explicit quality, budget, and diminishing-return gates.
bounded-exit.problem_solved: Revision loops either stop too early with a known high-impact defect or continue polishing low-value details indefinitely.
avoid_when: a mandatory validator has not yet passed
a hard defect requires escalation rather than iteration
the artifact is already accepted and no new requirement exists
bounded-exit.mechanism: Each pass evaluates the artifact against locked goals, chooses the single highest-value remaining defect, repairs it, and re-evaluates. Exit occurs on threshold satisfaction, budget exhaustion, or diminishing expected improvement; the historical acronym expansion is deliberately left unrecovered.
procedure: Lock acceptance criteria and a maximum pass or cost budget.
Score the current artifact against those criteria.
Choose the highest-impact repair that can be completed without reopening accepted decisions.
Apply the repair and record whether the target metric improved.
Stop when criteria pass, no repair has positive expected value, or the budget is reached; otherwise repeat.
always_do: define the exit condition before iterating
never_do: iterate merely because another rewrite is possible
use a quality score to waive a mandatory truth or safety check
invent an expansion for ExIt

interaction_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair supplies the smallest correction for the defect selected by the loop.
interaction_reasons.structured-refinement: Structured Refinement separates defect classes; Bounded ExIt decides whether another class-specific pass is worth doing.
interaction_reasons.parallel-qms: Parallel-QMS can score candidates or revisions on multiple quality dimensions before the exit decision.

counterbalance_reasons.reasoning-scale-controller: The scale controller can increase depth when risk justifies it, while Bounded ExIt prevents that depth from becoming unbounded.

redundancy_reasons.structured-refinement: Both organize revision, but Structured Refinement orders defect classes and Bounded ExIt owns continuation and termination.

conflict_rules: Mandatory acceptance checks outrank a pass budget; if budget expires first, return blocked rather than pass.
A newly discovered architecture failure hands off to Surgery or Regenerative Rewrite instead of repeating local passes.
failure_boundary: stopping with a known blocking defect
changing accepted decisions during a repair pass
optimizing an easy metric instead of the task
strong_model_may_skip: verbose pass logs for a one-pass correction
formal scoring when the next defect is obvious and low-risk

example.task_context: Revise a policy memo before publication.
example.why_activates: The memo is sound but can absorb an unknown number of polish passes.
example.inputs_state: Accuracy and required sections pass; one unclear paragraph and several optional style improvements remain; two passes are budgeted.
example.does: Repairs the unclear paragraph, rechecks the criteria, and exits because the remaining style gain is below its review cost.
example.does_not: Rewrite the whole memo or continue polishing synonyms after acceptance.
example.result: A publishable memo and an explicit diminishing-return exit.

distinctive_test.given: An artifact can always be improved a little more.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill selects the highest-value next repair and emits a reasoned stop decision tied to threshold, budget, or marginal value.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill says iterate until good without a measurable exit.

closest_neighbors.structured-refinement: Separates and sequences kinds of revision; Bounded ExIt controls whether revision continues.
closest_neighbors.reasoning-scale-controller: Chooses depth before or during work; Bounded ExIt terminates improvement passes.

bounded-exit.notes: Operational behavior is deeply recovered; only the historical expansion of the ExIt acronym remains unknown.

decision-first-scaffold.summary: Provisional scaffold that makes the decision to be produced explicit before collecting supporting analysis.
decision-first-scaffold.purpose: Keep analysis shaped around a decision, options, and decision criteria rather than accumulating directionless detail.
decision-first-scaffold.problem_solved: A solver can perform substantial analysis without defining what choice, recommendation, or commitment the analysis must support.
avoid_when: the task asks only for faithful extraction or description
the decision owner or available options are unknown
framing a decision would falsely narrow an exploratory task
decision-first-scaffold.mechanism: Modern conservative interpretation: write a decision sentence with owner, options, criteria, and deadline or commitment point; then admit analysis only when it changes an option score, exposes a constraint, or reduces a named uncertainty. The historical corpus recovers the exact name but not this mechanism.
procedure: State the decision in one sentence, including who will act.
List viable options, including defer or gather-more-evidence where legitimate.
Lock decision criteria and non-negotiable constraints.
Map each analysis question to a criterion or uncertainty.
Produce a recommendation with the evidence and unresolved uncertainty that drives it.
always_do: label the procedure as a modern interpretation
distinguish decision criteria from supporting information
preserve an explicit no-decision outcome when evidence is insufficient
never_do: claim the procedure is historically recovered
force a decision into a descriptive task
bury the actual decision below background analysis

interaction_reasons.task-set-lock-in: Task-Set Lock-In preserves the framed decision and constraints across a long run.
interaction_reasons.dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold: Driver isolation can identify which criterion should dominate the recommendation.

counterbalance_reasons.anti-tunnel-vision: Anti-Tunnel Vision prevents a decision-first frame from becoming first-option lock-in.

redundancy_reasons.task-set-lock-in: Both stabilize direction, but this provisional scaffold defines the decision while Task-Set Lock-In preserves an already defined task.

conflict_rules: If the user requests exploration without commitment, do not impose a final choice.
If evidence cannot support any option, return the missing evidence rather than a fabricated recommendation.
strong_model_may_skip: a formal decision matrix for a simple binary choice

example.task_context: Choose whether to migrate a service this quarter.
example.why_activates: The team has collected architecture notes without defining the commitment.
example.inputs_state: Two target platforms, a deadline, compliance constraints, and uncertain migration effort are known.
example.does: Frames the quarter-specific go/no-go decision, maps compliance, cost, and migration risk to the two options, and recommends a gated pilot.
example.does_not: Treat every platform fact as equally decision-relevant.
example.result: A criterion-linked recommendation with a named evidence gate.

distinctive_test.given: A request contains extensive background but no explicit choice frame.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill surfaces decision, owner, options, and criteria before analysis.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill only summarizes the background or asserts that its detailed procedure is recovered history.

closest_neighbors.task-set-lock-in: Preserves a chosen task set; Decision-First provisionally constructs the choice frame.
closest_neighbors.dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold: Finds the variable with greatest explanatory or outcome effect; Decision-First defines what outcome is being chosen.

decision-first-scaffold.notes: The exact historical name is recovered, but no historical operational definition was found in any of the three archived source documents. The included procedure is an explicitly modern, provisional interpretation.

dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold.summary: Provisional scaffold for identifying the smallest set of variables that accounts for most of an outcome.
dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold.purpose: Separate high-leverage causes or constraints from correlated, downstream, or low-impact factors.
dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold.problem_solved: When many causes are plausible, analysis can spread effort evenly and miss the factor that controls the decision or failure.
avoid_when: the system is known to require irreducibly joint causes
available evidence supports only correlation
the task requires a complete safety hazard inventory rather than prioritization
dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold.mechanism: Modern conservative interpretation: enumerate candidate drivers, define the target outcome, estimate each candidate's unique explanatory or intervention leverage, and test the leading driver against the strongest alternative and interaction effects. The historical sources recover only the scaffold's exact name.
procedure: Define the outcome and the time or system boundary.
List candidate drivers and distinguish causes, constraints, symptoms, and proxies.
Estimate each candidate's marginal effect using available comparisons, traces, or counterfactuals.
Test the leader against the strongest rival and check whether a pairwise interaction changes the ranking.
Select the dominant driver or report that no single driver is defensible; route effort accordingly.
always_do: state the target outcome before ranking drivers
test the top-ranked driver against at least one rival
never_do: claim single-cause dominance when evidence supports a coupled system
drop safety-critical minority risks
present the provisional mechanics as recovered

interaction_reasons.anti-tunnel-vision: Anti-Tunnel Vision supplies a rival-driver check against fixation.
interaction_reasons.critical-atomic-verification: Critical Atomic Verification can verify the key measurements on which driver ranking depends.

counterbalance_reasons.multi-layer-consistency: Multi-Layer Consistency checks whether local driver selection neglects a conflicting system-level dependency.

redundancy_reasons.anti-tunnel-vision: Both compare alternatives, but Driver Isolation ranks causal leverage while Anti-Tunnel Vision guards search breadth.

conflict_rules: A safety-critical factor is not discarded solely because its probability or average effect is lower.
If interaction terms dominate marginal effects, return a coupled-driver result rather than forcing one winner.
strong_model_may_skip: formal scoring when one measured bottleneck overwhelmingly dominates

example.why_activates: Price, onboarding failures, outages, and seasonality all correlate with churn.
example.inputs_state: Cohort data and incident timing permit marginal comparisons.
example.does: Defines 30-day churn, separates the onboarding failure cohort, compares it with price-change cohorts, and reports onboarding failure as dominant only after interaction checks.
example.does_not: Choose the most salient anecdote or suppress a smaller safety-related concern.
example.result: A defensible intervention priority and limits on the causal claim.

distinctive_test.given: Five plausible factors are listed for one outcome.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill estimates unique leverage, checks a rival and interactions, and permits a no-single-driver result.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill simply ranks factors by intuition or claims recovered details not present in the corpus.

closest_neighbors.anti-tunnel-vision: Protects alternative consideration; Driver Isolation ranks which cause actually carries the outcome.
closest_neighbors.decision-first-scaffold: Frames a choice; Driver Isolation identifies the causal or constraint variable most relevant to that choice.

dominant-driver-isolation-scaffold.notes: Exact name only. The operational content is an honest modern interpretation pending historical recovery.

forethought-checkpoints.summary: Places predictive checks immediately before costly, irreversible, or dependency-sensitive actions.
forethought-checkpoints.purpose: Catch missing prerequisites and foreseeable downstream failure while reversal is still cheap.
forethought-checkpoints.problem_solved: A locally valid next step can commit the workflow to an expensive path whose dependencies, blast radius, or rollback conditions were never checked.
avoid_when: reversible low-cost local edits
the checkpoint would duplicate an already enforced transaction guard
urgent containment requires a preauthorized emergency procedure
forethought-checkpoints.mechanism: At each consequential boundary, predict the most likely downstream failure, verify the prerequisite that would prevent it, define observable success and rollback, then commit and check the result. Checkpoints are placed by consequence rather than at every trivial step.
procedure: Identify the next irreversible, high-cost, or dependency-sensitive action.
Name the plausible downstream failure and affected dependency.
Verify prerequisites, authority, backups, and rollback path proportionate to risk.
Define the immediate post-action observation that indicates success or failure.
Commit only if the checkpoint passes, then inspect the result before continuing.
always_do: tie each checkpoint to a concrete consequence
never_do: turn every minor step into ceremonial review
treat a prediction as verified fact
continue past a failed prerequisite without escalation

interaction_reasons.risk-tier-scaling: Risk Tier Scaling determines how deep the checkpoint must be.
interaction_reasons.bounded-exit: Bounded ExIt prevents repeated checkpoint analysis once required evidence and safeguards are sufficient.

counterbalance_reasons.proportionality: Proportionality keeps checkpoint overhead aligned to actual consequence.

redundancy_reasons.risk-tier-scaling: Risk tier sets rigor globally; Forethought performs the concrete pre-commit prediction and prerequisite check.

conflict_rules: A failed hard prerequisite blocks commitment regardless of schedule pressure.
During urgent containment, use the approved emergency checkpoint rather than omitting checks entirely.
failure_boundary: analysis after commitment instead of before
strong_model_may_skip: explicit checkpoint prose for a fully reversible in-memory operation
strong_model_keep: pre-commit prerequisite check for consequential actions

example.why_activates: The change can break downstream consumers and is costly to reverse after rollout.
example.inputs_state: Consumer inventory, compatibility plan, telemetry, and rollback deployment exist.
example.does: Verifies consumer migration, stages compatibility, sets an error-rate threshold, deploys, and checks telemetry before removing the old field.
example.does_not: Approve the rename because the local service tests pass.
example.result: A gated rollout with evidence before irreversible cleanup.

distinctive_test.given: A workflow is about to perform a costly dependency-sensitive action.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill predicts a downstream failure, checks its prerequisite and rollback, commits, then observes.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill offers only a generic caution or performs review after the irreversible step.

closest_neighbors.risk-tier-scaling: Selects rigor according to risk; Forethought installs a check at a specific commitment boundary.
closest_neighbors.bounded-exit: Decides when iterative repair stops; Forethought decides whether a consequential next action may begin.

forethought-checkpoints.notes: The catalog recovers the anticipate → verify prerequisite → commit → check result sequence.

multiverse-reasoning.summary: Creates two or three materially different solution worlds, evaluates each against one shared rubric, and commits to one result while retiring the rest.
multiverse-reasoning.purpose: Obtain real alternative search without losing control of truth, constraints, cost, or convergence.
multiverse-reasoning.problem_solved: A single-path solver can overfit its first plan; an unconstrained multi-agent or brainstorming process can instead proliferate branches without a defensible collapse.
avoid_when: a locked source dictates a single faithful transformation
one hard constraint eliminates all but one path
the task is too small for branch overhead
multiverse-reasoning.mechanism: Open exactly two or three branch records that differ in strategy, causal model, or architecture. Give every branch the same locked facts, requirements, risk limits, and evaluation rubric; develop each only far enough to expose its decisive tradeoffs. Score them, apply hard vetoes before soft preferences, select or synthesize one committed path, and mark every losing branch retired so its assumptions cannot leak into execution.
procedure: Lock shared facts, goals, constraints, risk boundaries, and a branch budget of two or three.
Define branches with a one-sentence strategy, distinctive assumption, predicted advantage, and disconfirming condition.
Develop each branch to the same decision depth; do not let the favored branch consume the entire budget.
Evaluate all branches on the same dimensions, such as truth, requirement coverage, coherence, cost, risk, and reversibility.
Veto any branch that violates a hard constraint, then select the strongest survivor or synthesize only compatible components.
Emit one committed plan plus a retirement record naming rejected branches and why they must not influence downstream work.
always_do: apply hard constraints before aggregate scores
never_do: create unbounded universes
score one branch on easier criteria
blend mutually inconsistent assumptions during synthesis
carry losing-branch instructions into the chosen execution state

interaction_reasons.parallel-qms: Parallel-QMS provides the shared multidimensional scoring and collapse gate.
interaction_reasons.anti-tunnel-vision: Anti-Tunnel Vision audits whether branch diversity is real and whether the favorite was preselected.
interaction_reasons.task-set-lock-in: Task-Set Lock-In gives all branches identical goals and non-negotiable constraints.

counterbalance_reasons.bounded-exit: Bounded ExIt prevents branch development or comparison from continuing after the decision value falls below cost.
counterbalance_reasons.neuro-focus: After collapse, Neuro-Focus narrows execution to the selected universe.

redundancy_reasons.anti-tunnel-vision: Both counter first-path fixation; Multiverse manages full candidate state and collapse, while Anti-Tunnel can be a lighter rival check.
redundancy_reasons.parallel-qms: QMS evaluates alternatives but does not itself generate or retire branch worlds.

conflict_rules: A hard truth, safety, or authorization veto cannot be outvoted by soft quality scores.
Synthesis is allowed only when selected components share compatible assumptions and interfaces.
If no branch passes, return the blocking constraint or request evidence rather than select the least-invalid branch.
failure_boundary: majority voting over a hard veto
strong_model_may_skip: separate long-form prose for every branch when compact branch records expose the tradeoffs

example.task_context: Design a community skill repository contribution model.
example.why_activates: Central curation, open pull requests, and federated registries have materially different trust and maintenance tradeoffs.
example.inputs_state: Public accessibility, vendor neutrality, provenance, and low maintainer burden are locked criteria.
example.does: Builds three compact branch records, evaluates each against the same governance and usability rubric, vetoes the federation branch if discoverability cannot be guaranteed, and selects an open-PR model with automated validation.
example.does_not: Call three slightly different pull-request workflows separate universes or retain federation-only assumptions in the chosen plan.
example.result: One executable governance plan with two retired alternatives and explicit reasons.

distinctive_test.given: A task has several credible approaches.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill creates 2–3 materially distinct branches under shared constraints, evaluates uniformly, commits to one outcome, and retires losers.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill merely brainstorms options, uses cosmetic variants, or leaves multiple active plans after selection.

closest_neighbors.anti-tunnel-vision: A lightweight guard against fixation; Multiverse maintains explicit branch state through evaluation and collapse.
closest_neighbors.parallel-qms: Scores candidates; Multiverse owns candidate generation, branch isolation, and retirement.
closest_neighbors.reasoning-scale-controller: Chooses reasoning depth; Multiverse chooses among distinct solution worlds at the selected depth.

multiverse-reasoning.notes: Both core catalog behavior and Paper-Author use are recovered: 2–3 meaningfully distinct plans, common quality dimensions, controlled commitment, and bounded collapse.

phase-locked-reasoning-scaffold.summary: Keeps recovered semantic phases separate so factual, evidentiary, probabilistic, and heuristic claims do not silently substitute for one another.
phase-locked-reasoning-scaffold.purpose: Prevent cross-phase contamination while still allowing explicitly governed transitions between reasoning modes.
phase-locked-reasoning-scaffold.problem_solved: A plausible interpretation or heuristic can be written as a fact, or an evidence-management step can drift into unsupported synthesis, when phase boundaries are implicit.
best_fit_tasks: long workflows with distinct reasoning modes
avoid_when: a single atomic transformation has no phase transition
phase labels would add more complexity than the task
the underlying source classification is itself unknown
phase-locked-reasoning-scaffold.mechanism: Assign each working claim to the recovered semantic phase appropriate to its status, keep phase-specific operations and admissible transformations explicit, and require a labeled transition when a claim moves from evidence or fact into interpretation, probability, or heuristic use. The exact scaffold mechanics are derived from recovered semantic phase separation; they are not directly preserved as a historical procedure.
procedure: Declare the phases needed for the task and what claim types each admits.
Tag inputs and intermediate claims with their current phase.
Within a phase, perform only operations allowed for that claim type.
At a transition, record the source claim, transformation, assumptions, and destination phase.
Before output, audit that interpretations, probabilities, and heuristics are not stated as source facts.
always_do: audit the final wording against claim status
never_do: allow an interpretation to overwrite its source fact
treat phase separation as a license to ignore cross-phase consistency
claim the normalized procedure is verbatim historical recovery

interaction_reasons.domain-mode-isolation: Domain/Mode Isolation prevents rules from one operational mode from leaking into another; phase locking does the same for semantic claim status.
interaction_reasons.citation-fidelity: Citation Fidelity anchors factual and evidentiary phases to their sources.

counterbalance_reasons.multi-layer-consistency: Consistency checks ensure that separation does not permit mutually contradictory claims to coexist across phases.

redundancy_reasons.domain-mode-isolation: Both isolate contexts, but phase locking separates semantic status inside a workflow while domain-mode isolation separates broader operating modes.

conflict_rules: A transition cannot increase certainty beyond its evidence without an explicit warrant.
When phase-specific outputs conflict, factual and source-locked constraints take precedence and the conflict remains visible.
failure_boundary: isolated phases that evade global consistency
strong_model_may_skip: printing phase labels when the task is one-step and claim status is unambiguous
strong_model_keep: explicit transition warrants for consequential inference

example.task_context: Summarize evidence for a policy outcome.
example.why_activates: The sources report observations, while the requested conclusion requires interpretation and uncertainty.
example.inputs_state: Quoted findings, study limitations, and stakeholder heuristics are available.
example.does: Keeps reported findings in the factual/evidentiary phase, labels the synthesis as interpretation, and states probability without converting it into fact.
example.does_not: Attribute the synthesized policy conclusion directly to a source that did not make it.
example.result: A readable conclusion whose evidence, inference, and uncertainty remain distinguishable.

distinctive_test.given: A source fact is used to support a probabilistic recommendation.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill records and labels the transition rather than presenting the recommendation as quoted fact.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill either mixes statuses silently or walls phases off without checking consistency.

closest_neighbors.domain-mode-isolation: Separates operational domains or modes; Phase-Locked separates semantic claim statuses.
closest_neighbors.citation-fidelity: Protects source attribution; Phase-Locked additionally governs inference beyond the source.

reasoning-scale-controller.summary: Selects the smallest adequate reasoning scale from fact-level inspection through global architecture, then changes scale only on explicit complexity or risk signals.
reasoning-scale-controller.purpose: Match reasoning depth and scope to the unit of work instead of applying either shallow local analysis or system-wide architecture indiscriminately.
reasoning-scale-controller.problem_solved: Models overthink simple transformations, underthink coupled high-risk tasks, or mix local sentence repair with global architecture decisions.
avoid_when: a governing workflow already fixes the required scale
the unit is safety-critical and policy mandates the highest review tier
scale labels would replace rather than guide actual reasoning
reasoning-scale-controller.mechanism: Route work through one controller: Subatomic for a fact, local relation, constraint, or sentence decision; Atomic for a small verified inference or action; Nano as a light intermediate structure whose detailed historical spec remains unrecovered; Micro for task-local scaffolds and dependencies; QMS for quality evaluation; Cosmic for global architecture, strategy, or long-horizon planning. Escalate when dependency span, ambiguity, irreversibility, or risk exceeds the current scale; de-escalate after the larger question is resolved.
procedure: Identify the unit of work, dependency radius, uncertainty, and consequence of error.
Choose the lowest scale that can represent all relevant dependencies.
Execute only the operations appropriate to that scale.
Escalate one or more levels when local reasoning exposes unresolved cross-unit dependencies, competing quality dimensions, or global architecture effects.
After the higher-scale decision, return local implementation to the smallest adequate scale and record the boundary.
always_do: start at the smallest adequate scale
escalate on concrete signals rather than prestige
preserve global constraints when returning to local work
keep Nano semantics modest because its detailed historical specification is unrecovered
never_do: use Cosmic for a sentence edit
solve architecture from isolated facts without aggregation
invent a detailed historical Nano algorithm
confuse QMS evaluation with generation

interaction_reasons.cognitive-governor: The governor budgets effort after the scale controller identifies the required scope.
interaction_reasons.dynamic-depth-allocation: Dynamic allocation varies effort within the selected scale as evidence and difficulty change.
interaction_reasons.micro-scaffolding: Micro-Scaffolding structures task-local dependencies when the controller selects Micro scale.

counterbalance_reasons.bounded-exit: Bounded ExIt caps repeated work at any selected scale.
counterbalance_reasons.critical-atomic-verification: Atomic verification prevents scale escalation from resting on bad fact-level units.

redundancy_reasons.dynamic-depth-allocation: Both tune reasoning effort, but the scale controller selects semantic scope while dynamic allocation adjusts depth or budget.

conflict_rules: Risk-mandated review overrides the desire to stay at a cheaper scale.
Cosmic conclusions must be decomposed back into verifiable local units before execution.
Nano may be used only as a light intermediate label until historical mechanics are recovered.
failure_boundary: local reasoning that ignores global dependencies
strong_model_may_skip: printing scale names on routine tasks
stepping through every intermediate scale when direct routing is obvious

example.task_context: Correct one citation in a long report whose architecture is already accepted.
example.why_activates: The surrounding artifact is large, but the actual defect is local and source-verifiable.
example.inputs_state: The correct source passage and locked report structure are available.
example.does: Routes source verification to Subatomic, the citation replacement to Atomic, and avoids Cosmic redesign unless the correction exposes a section-wide provenance failure.
example.does_not: Re-outline the report because the document is long.
example.result: A proportional local correction with an explicit escalation condition.

distinctive_test.expect: The skill chooses a local scale, states the signal for escalation, and returns from any global review to local execution.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill always applies maximum depth or treats scale names as decorative labels.

closest_neighbors.dynamic-depth-allocation: Adjusts effort intensity; Reasoning Scale Controller chooses the semantic size of the unit being reasoned over.
closest_neighbors.cognitive-governor: Controls budget and limits; Scale Controller routes scope.
closest_neighbors.micro-scaffolding: Executes planning at Micro scale; Scale Controller decides when that scale is needed.

contradiction-micro-repair.summary: Repairs the smallest region responsible for a contradiction and rechecks both statements without rewriting unrelated content.
contradiction-micro-repair.purpose: Resolve direct logical or factual inconsistency while preserving every compatible claim and locked constraint.
contradiction-micro-repair.problem_solved: A document or state can contain two claims that cannot both hold, yet broad rewriting risks erasing the supported one or creating new drift.
best_fit_tasks: state snapshots with mutually exclusive flags
documents whose conclusion contradicts a cited premise
avoid_when: the apparent contradiction is a legitimate difference in scope or time
the conflict spans the artifact's governing architecture
neither side can be adjudicated from available authority
contradiction-micro-repair.mechanism: Represent the conflict as claim A, claim B, and the condition under which they cannot coexist; inspect scope, time, modality, and authority to decide whether it is real. If real and locally adjudicable, patch only the unsupported or misstated unit, then retest the pair and nearby dependents. If authority is insufficient, preserve the conflict explicitly instead of choosing by fluency.
procedure: Extract the two conflicting claims and their provenance.
Normalize their scope, time, subject, quantity, and modality to confirm a true contradiction.
Determine which claim is locked, better supported, or requires escalation.
Edit the smallest clause, field, or local rule that resolves the inconsistency.
Re-evaluate both claims and any directly dependent conclusion; report unresolved conflict when evidence cannot adjudicate.
always_do: preserve the better-supported or locked claim
recheck both sides and direct dependents
never_do: flatten legitimate perspectives into one claim
silently choose a side without authority
rewrite unrelated sections to make the artifact sound consistent

interaction_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair supplies the minimal patch discipline after the contradiction is localized.
interaction_reasons.bidirectional-consistency: Bidirectional Consistency can detect whether upstream and downstream claims disagree in both directions.

counterbalance_reasons.multi-truth-gating: Multi-Truth Gating prevents repair when claims are merely different scoped truths rather than contradictions.

outputs: minimal adjudicated patch or explicit unresolved conflict
failure_boundary: repair that leaves a dependent contradiction
strong_model_may_skip: formal claim notation when the conflict is an obvious local typo

example.task_context: A report says a pilot starts in June and later says it concluded in May of the same year.
example.why_activates: The dates are mutually incompatible under the same pilot identity and year.
example.inputs_state: The approved schedule says the pilot starts in March and ends in May; the June sentence is generated prose.
example.does: Confirms same scope and year, replaces June with March in the single clause, and rechecks the timeline and conclusion.
example.does_not: Rewrite the entire schedule section or preserve both dates as perspectives.

crispr-edit.summary: Applies a precisely bounded change to an OS, prompt, skill, document, or architecture while proving that named invariants outside the edit remain intact.
crispr-edit.purpose: Make high-confidence micro-edits to structured systems without collateral semantic or interface drift.
crispr-edit.problem_solved: Even a small requested change can accidentally alter neighboring rules, precedence, identifiers, citations, schemas, or behavior when treated as free-form rewriting.
best_fit_tasks: one rule change in a prompt or skill
avoid_when: the governing structure is wrong
multiple interfaces must be redesigned
the target boundary cannot be isolated
the requested change conflicts with locked truth or policy
crispr-edit.mechanism: Construct a patch contract before editing: exact target coordinates, requested semantic delta, protected invariants, allowed collateral region, and validation probes. Snapshot the target plus its immediate dependency boundary, apply the smallest diff that realizes the delta, and compare before/after behavior on both the changed case and invariant cases. A patch that requires broad remapping is rejected and escalated to Surgery rather than stretched into disguised rewrite.
procedure: Identify the exact editable unit and the request's semantic delta.
Enumerate invariants: facts, IDs, interfaces, precedence, citations, unaffected behaviors, and formatting contracts that must not change.
Trace immediate inbound and outbound dependencies to set a finite collateral boundary.
Create and apply the smallest patch inside that boundary.
Run a positive probe for the new behavior and negative probes for each protected invariant.
Inspect the diff for unrelated changes; accept, revert-and-redesign, or escalate to Surgery if the boundary cannot hold.
always_do: declare target and invariants before editing
test both the intended change and unchanged behaviors
never_do: use search-and-replace without checking semantic scope
rename or reorder unrelated elements for cleanliness
claim success from syntax alone
continue expanding the patch boundary until it becomes a macro rewrite

interaction_reasons.invariance-stress-scaffold: Invariance Stress turns the protected set into explicit negative tests.
interaction_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair is the lighter local repair discipline used inside a CRISPR patch.
interaction_reasons.critical-atomic-verification: Atomic verification validates the exact facts, tokens, or rules touched.

counterbalance_reasons.surgery-edit: Surgery takes over when the edit cannot preserve the current architecture or interfaces within a bounded region.

redundancy_reasons.micro-repair: Both minimize change, but CRISPR adds a structured target contract, dependency boundary, and invariant test matrix for OS-like artifacts.
redundancy_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite protects facts during prose transformation; CRISPR applies a precise semantic patch to any structured artifact.

conflict_rules: Locked safety, truth, and authorization invariants cannot be included in the requested delta.
If the new behavior and protected invariants cannot coexist, stop and expose the conflict.
If more than the bounded dependency region must change, route to Surgery with a migration plan.
failure_boundary: syntactically valid but behaviorally wrong patch
strong_model_may_skip: a long written patch contract for a trivial typo with no dependencies

micro-repair.summary: Corrects the smallest faulty unit while freezing all correct surrounding content.
micro-repair.purpose: Restore local correctness or completeness with the minimum semantic blast radius.
micro-repair.problem_solved: Models often answer a one-clause, one-transition, or one-format defect with a wholesale rewrite that damages accepted material.
avoid_when: the artifact architecture is globally wrong
the same defect repeats systemically
the correct local replacement depends on unresolved global decisions
micro-repair.mechanism: Define a repair window around the smallest unit that fails an explicit criterion, freeze the surrounding accepted region, patch only that unit and any directly required connective token, then compare the window before and after. Widen once only when a direct dependency proves the first window insufficient; recurring or architecture-level failure escalates instead of allowing scope creep.
procedure: Identify the exact failed criterion and the smallest text, field, rule, or code unit causing it.
Mark the surrounding accepted content and locked facts as frozen.
Draft the smallest replacement that satisfies the criterion.
Check boundary coherence with the immediately preceding and following units.
Verify the target defect is gone and no frozen atom changed.
If repair requires broad movement or repeats elsewhere, stop and route to Structured Refinement, Regenerative Rewrite, or Surgery.
never_do: rewrite for style outside the repair window
expand scope because adjacent prose could also be improved
use local repair to conceal systemic failure

interaction_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite preserves factual atoms when the micro-repair changes wording.
interaction_reasons.invariance-stress-scaffold: Invariance Stress verifies frozen neighbors and facts remain unchanged.
interaction_reasons.contradiction-micro-repair: The contradiction pack adds conflict adjudication when the localized defect is inconsistency.

counterbalance_reasons.regenerative-rewrite: Regenerative Rewrite is the correct escalation when local patches cannot restore global structure.
counterbalance_reasons.surgery-edit: Surgery replaces architecture when the defect is structural rather than local.

redundancy_reasons.crispr-edit: Both are precise; Micro-Repair is the general smallest-fault correction, while CRISPR uses a formal patch contract for structured systems.
redundancy_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite governs dimensions of prose transformation; Micro-Repair governs defect scope.

conflict_rules: Do not preserve a frozen neighbor if it is proven part of the defect; explicitly widen the window instead.
A locked invariant outranks local fluency.
After one justified scope expansion, recurring failure triggers escalation rather than further widening.
failure_boundary: repair that breaks a neighboring transition
serial local patches to a global architecture failure

regenerative-rewrite.summary: Rebuilds an artifact from its locked truths and constraints when local repairs cannot recover global coherence or source mapping.
regenerative-rewrite.purpose: Replace a systemically broken expression or structure without losing verified content, requirements, provenance, or accepted decisions.
regenerative-rewrite.problem_solved: An artifact can be locally polished yet remain globally incoherent because its architecture is wrong, sections conflict, or evidence-to-claim mapping has collapsed.
avoid_when: one sentence or field is wrong
the existing architecture is sound
locked atoms and provenance cannot yet be separated from generated content
regenerative-rewrite.mechanism: Quarantine the failed artifact, extract a ledger of verified facts, citations, requirements, decisions, and protected wording, and design a fresh structure from that ledger rather than editing the old prose in place. Reintroduce each locked atom with provenance, validate global coherence and coverage, and compare against the ledger—not against the failed wording—as the acceptance baseline.
procedure: Demonstrate systemic failure: wrong architecture, cross-section contradiction, or broken source mapping that resists bounded repair.
Extract and classify locked facts, citations, constraints, requirements, and accepted decisions.
Set the failed draft aside and create a new outline or artifact structure from the locked ledger.
Rebuild content section by section, attaching every factual claim to its source or ledger atom.
Validate requirement coverage, global coherence, citation mapping, and absence of imported failed assumptions.
Compare the rebuilt artifact with the locked ledger and record intentionally discarded generated material.
always_do: build a locked-atom ledger before rewriting
reconstruct from verified state rather than memory of the old prose
never_do: use regeneration for one awkward sentence
discard accepted decisions because the wording is inconvenient
copy incoherent passages wholesale into the new structure
claim historical wording was preserved when only semantics were locked

interaction_reasons.task-set-lock-in: Task-Set Lock-In preserves the goals and requirements during reconstruction.
interaction_reasons.surgery-edit: Surgery can replace the artifact's architecture before Regenerative Rewrite repopulates it.
interaction_reasons.citation-fidelity: Citation Fidelity ensures the rebuilt claims remain mapped to original sources.

counterbalance_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair should be tried first for bounded defects and prevents unnecessary regeneration.

redundancy_reasons.surgery-edit: Both address macro failure, but Surgery changes structural interfaces while Regenerative Rewrite reconstructs content from locked truth and constraints.

conflict_rules: Verified facts, citations, and non-negotiable requirements survive even if they complicate the new structure.
If the architecture alone is defective, Surgery may define the replacement skeleton; regeneration then fills it.
If no reliable locked ledger can be formed, stop for source recovery rather than regenerate from guesses.
strong_model_may_skip: verbose quarantine ceremony when the failed draft is already versioned

example.does_not: Polish each old section in sequence or carry unsupported transitions into the rebuild.
example.result: A coherent report whose claims map back to verified source atoms.

distinctive_test.expect: The skill proves local insufficiency, extracts locked atoms, sets aside the failed wording, and reconstructs against the ledger.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill performs a large paraphrase of the old draft or invokes regeneration for a single local defect.

closest_neighbors.micro-repair: Changes one faulty unit; Regenerative Rewrite rebuilds when many local patches cannot restore the whole.
closest_neighbors.surgery-edit: Replaces macro architecture and interfaces; Regenerative Rewrite reconstructs artifact content from locked state.

safe-rewrite.summary: Changes only requested presentation dimensions while preserving locked meaning, facts, constraints, names, numbers, dates, quotes, and citations.
safe-rewrite.purpose: Make paraphrase, polish, tone, or formatting safe by treating content atoms as invariants rather than suggestions.
safe-rewrite.problem_solved: Fluent rewriting can introduce factual drift, altered modality, citation mismatch, or lost requirements even when the request is purely stylistic.
avoid_when: the user asks to change substantive meaning
the source is internally contradictory and needs adjudication
global structure is broken
safe-rewrite.mechanism: Extract a before-state ledger of factual and constraint atoms, mark the dimensions authorized to change, perform the rewrite only along those dimensions, then compare names, numbers, dates, quotes, citations, modality, requirements, and causal claims. Any atom difference not explicitly authorized is reverted or surfaced for approval.
procedure: Identify authorized change dimensions such as tone, length, format, or reading level.
Extract locked atoms: claims, entities, numbers, dates, quotations, citations, requirements, negations, and uncertainty markers.
Rewrite without adding evidence or changing the locked atoms.
Diff the rewritten artifact against the atom ledger and inspect citation-to-claim fit.
Restore unauthorized changes and report any requested transformation that cannot preserve meaning.
always_do: separate semantic atoms from surface form
recheck citations against the rewritten claims
never_do: add plausible facts for smoothness
alter numbers or named entities silently
turn qualified language into certainty
move a citation so it appears to support a different claim

interaction_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair bounds the rewritten region when only one passage is defective.
interaction_reasons.citation-fidelity: Citation Fidelity performs the source-to-claim validation required after wording changes.
interaction_reasons.style-alignment: Style Alignment specifies one authorized surface dimension while Safe Rewrite protects semantics.

counterbalance_reasons.regenerative-rewrite: Regenerative Rewrite is needed when preservation of the old structure prevents a coherent result.

redundancy_reasons.style-alignment: Style Alignment selects the target voice; Safe Rewrite is the preservation guard across any transformation dimension.
redundancy_reasons.crispr-edit: CRISPR changes a named semantic rule while preserving other invariants; Safe Rewrite generally forbids semantic change and transforms expression.

conflict_rules: Truth and locked constraints outrank requested style.
If shortening would remove a required qualification, keep the qualification or report the conflict.
Exact quotations remain exact unless the user authorizes conversion to paraphrase.
strong_model_may_skip: printing the full atom ledger for a tiny rewrite

example.inputs_state: The update contains three metrics, one date, two caveats, and a citation.

example.does_not: Round the numbers, drop uncertainty, or add a business implication absent from the source.

distinctive_test.expect: The skill locks semantic atoms, transforms only tone and length, and compares sensitive facts and citations afterward.

closest_neighbors.micro-repair: Limits a correction to the faulty unit; Safe Rewrite limits which dimensions may change.

structured-refinement.summary: Revises an artifact in ordered, non-mixing passes: factual correction, structural repair, style repair, then final validation.
structured-refinement.purpose: Prevent one revision pass from trading away correctness while improving structure or style.
structured-refinement.problem_solved: Mixed editing objectives make it hard to know whether factual, structural, and stylistic defects were fixed or newly introduced.
best_fit_tasks: reports requiring source and style review
avoid_when: only one bounded defect exists
the artifact requires complete regeneration
the source truth is not yet established
structured-refinement.mechanism: Classify defects before editing and run passes in dependency order: facts and source mapping first, structure and requirement coverage second, style and pedagogy third, final validation last. Accepted decisions are locked between passes, and a later pass may not silently reopen an earlier one.
procedure: Inventory defects and assign each to factual, structural, stylistic, or validation class.
Correct facts, citations, and locked constraints; freeze the accepted semantic ledger.
Repair ordering, dependencies, section roles, and requirement coverage without changing the frozen facts.
Adjust voice, clarity, and pedagogy without changing facts or structure except where explicitly authorized.
Run an independent final check across all classes and use Bounded ExIt to decide whether another pass is justified.
always_do: fix upstream factual issues before downstream polish
never_do: combine fact correction and free stylistic invention
let a later pass silently undo an earlier one
polish a structure already known to be globally invalid

interaction_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite protects frozen semantics during style and format passes.
interaction_reasons.bounded-exit: Bounded ExIt decides whether another class-specific pass has sufficient value.
interaction_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair implements each localized correction selected within a pass.

counterbalance_reasons.regenerative-rewrite: Regeneration replaces the entire cycle when architecture or source mapping is systemically unrecoverable.

redundancy_reasons.bounded-exit: Both govern iteration, but Structured Refinement defines pass content and order while Bounded ExIt controls continuation.
redundancy_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite is one preservation rule used inside multiple refinement passes.

conflict_rules: Factual correctness outranks structural elegance and style.
A later pass that discovers an upstream defect returns explicitly to the relevant pass and revalidates downstream results.
If the defect inventory shows architecture failure, stop the cycle and escalate.
strong_model_may_skip: physically separate drafts for each pass when an auditable diff is available

example.does_not: Rewrite the dated sentences for tone before establishing correct dates.

distinctive_test.reject: The skill performs one blended rewrite or iterates without pass boundaries.

closest_neighbors.micro-repair: Executes one small correction; Structured Refinement coordinates many corrections across defect classes.

surgery-edit.summary: Replaces or reorganizes architecture-level structures through an explicit cutover and migration plan when a bounded CRISPR patch cannot work.
surgery-edit.purpose: Make macro changes to layers, cores, workflows, or incompatible interfaces without losing invariants, dependents, or rollback control.
surgery-edit.problem_solved: Large structural changes fail when treated as accumulated local edits: hidden interfaces break, old and new architectures coexist ambiguously, and rollback becomes impossible.
avoid_when: a localized invariant-preserving patch suffices
the replacement architecture lacks acceptance criteria
migration or rollback cannot be made safe
the desired outcome is only prose polish
surgery-edit.mechanism: Declare the failing structural boundary and why CRISPR cannot preserve it, inventory every inbound and outbound interface, and define a replacement architecture with mapped invariants. Plan old-to-new state migration, adapters, staged cutover, observability, and rollback; change the structure in bounded phases, validate each dependent contract, then remove the old path only after the replacement passes global checks.
procedure: Document the architecture-level failure and evidence that local editing is insufficient.
Inventory components, state, public and internal interfaces, dependents, precedence rules, and invariants.
Design the replacement structure and map every old responsibility and interface to retain, adapt, retire, or explicitly reject.
Define migration order, compatibility adapters, checkpoints, observability, rollback, and cutover criteria.
Implement or specify the replacement in stages while validating each interface and state transfer.
Cut over only when criteria pass; remove the old structure, audit for orphaned references, and record irreversible decisions.
never_do: invoke Surgery for a local defect
replace structure without a responsibility map
run old and new precedence rules ambiguously
remove the old path before dependent contracts pass

interaction_reasons.regenerative-rewrite: Regenerative Rewrite can repopulate a replaced structure from locked truth after Surgery defines the new architecture.
interaction_reasons.task-set-lock-in: Task-Set Lock-In preserves objectives and non-negotiable invariants across the migration.
interaction_reasons.forethought-checkpoints: Forethought gates irreversible cutover and retirement steps.

counterbalance_reasons.crispr-edit: CRISPR is preferred when the change fits a bounded invariant-preserving patch and prevents unnecessary surgery.
counterbalance_reasons.micro-repair: Micro-Repair handles isolated defects without architecture disruption.

redundancy_reasons.regenerative-rewrite: Both operate globally; Surgery changes structural components and interfaces, while Regenerative Rewrite rebuilds content against a locked ledger.

conflict_rules: Use CRISPR when all required behavior can coexist with current interfaces inside a bounded patch.
A hard invariant without a valid old-to-new mapping blocks cutover.
If rollback is impossible, raise the validation threshold and obtain explicit authority before commitment.
failure_boundary: macro edit disguised as patch accumulation
strong_model_may_skip: a heavyweight migration document for an internal, versioned, fully reversible refactor

example.does_not: Patch conditionals into the old loader until it accidentally behaves like two architectures.

distinctive_test.reject: The skill applies an expanding local patch, produces only a new diagram, or removes the old structure before dependents pass.

closest_neighbors.crispr-edit: A bounded precise patch preserving architecture; Surgery replaces architecture and migrates its interfaces.
closest_neighbors.regenerative-rewrite: Reconstructs content from locked truth; Surgery reconstructs structural organization and contracts.
closest_neighbors.micro-repair: Repairs one faulty unit; Surgery operates only when the unit boundaries themselves must change.

surgery-edit.notes: The recovered source clearly reserves Surgery for layer reorganization, Core replacement, major workflow changes, and incompatible refactors when CRISPR is insufficient.

explanation-minimality-scaffold.summary: Modern operationalization that emits the smallest explanation sufficient for the reader to understand, trust, and act on the answer.
explanation-minimality-scaffold.purpose: Remove explanatory material that does not change comprehension, verification, decision, or safe execution while retaining required rationale and caveats.
explanation-minimality-scaffold.problem_solved: Verbose explanations hide the answer and decision-relevant constraints, but blind shortening can remove the causal bridge, evidence, or warning a reader needs.
avoid_when: the user requests a tutorial or exhaustive rationale
high-stakes action requires full assumptions and warnings
a novel argument needs its derivation to be auditable
explanation-minimality-scaffold.mechanism: Set an explanation contract consisting of the outcome, the minimum causal or evidentiary bridge, required caveats, and the next action. Draft those blocks first, then test every additional sentence with a deletion probe: if removal does not impair correctness, comprehension, verification, safety, or actionability for the target reader, delete it. This mechanism is modern; only the exact historical scaffold name was recovered.
procedure: Identify the reader, requested depth, decision or action, and risk tier.
List mandatory explanation blocks: answer, indispensable why, evidence or method needed for trust, caveats, and next action.
Draft one compact block for each mandatory need.
Run a deletion probe sentence by sentence against correctness, comprehension, verification, safety, and actionability.
Restore any deleted bridge whose absence creates a knowledge jump; stop when remaining content is necessary or explicitly requested.
always_do: include enough bridge for the target reader to verify or follow the result
never_do: equate minimality with unexplained assertion
remove safety or uncertainty language for brevity
repeat the same conclusion in several formats without need
claim this procedure is historically recovered

interaction_reasons.pedagogical-alignment: Pedagogical Alignment defines what the reader needs before Minimality removes surplus explanation.
interaction_reasons.bounded-exit: Bounded ExIt supplies the recovered marginal-value stop principle for further polishing.

counterbalance_reasons.citation-fidelity: Citation Fidelity prevents compression from detaching claims from required source support.

redundancy_reasons.pedagogical-alignment: Both shape explanation, but pedagogy adapts conceptual accessibility while minimality controls how much explanatory material survives.

conflict_rules: User-requested detail and risk-mandated disclosure override brevity.
When a deletion creates ambiguity about scope, uncertainty, or authority, restore the qualifying content.
Citation or evidence requirements are not optional surplus.
strong_model_may_skip: an explicit deletion log
formal block labels in the final response

pedagogical-alignment.summary: Matches conceptual granularity, terminology, sequencing, and examples to the reader while preserving full technical accuracy.
pedagogical-alignment.purpose: Make correct content learnable and usable for a specified audience without diluting claims or inventing simplifications.
pedagogical-alignment.problem_solved: An explanation can be accurate but inaccessible because it assumes missing prerequisites, uses undefined jargon, or presents abstractions before concrete anchors.
avoid_when: the audience and purpose cannot be inferred and the choice materially changes content
exact legal or technical wording must remain verbatim
simplification would conceal decision-relevant uncertainty
pedagogical-alignment.mechanism: Build a compact audience model—known prerequisites, target capability, jargon tolerance, and action context—then choose the smallest conceptual steps that bridge from that model to the target. Define or replace jargon at first use, order prerequisite before dependent ideas, add an example only where it resolves a likely misconception, and run an accuracy-backcheck against the unsimplified claim.
procedure: Identify the reader's likely starting knowledge and the capability they need after reading.
List prerequisites and terms that the explanation currently assumes.
Sequence content from familiar anchor through the minimum conceptual bridge to the target.
Define necessary jargon or replace it with accurate plain language; add a representative example where abstraction alone is likely to fail.
Back-check every simplification, analogy, and example against the original technical claim and retain important limitations.
always_do: check analogies for where they break
never_do: talk down to the reader
remove uncertainty or boundary conditions to sound simple
use an analogy that changes the mechanism
assume more domain knowledge than the audience model supports

interaction_reasons.explanation-minimality-scaffold: Minimality removes surplus after Pedagogical Alignment determines which conceptual bridges the reader actually needs.
interaction_reasons.style-alignment: Style Alignment matches authorized voice while pedagogy matches comprehension needs.

counterbalance_reasons.citation-fidelity: Citation Fidelity keeps adapted explanations tied to evidence when wording and examples change.

redundancy_reasons.style-alignment: Both adapt output, but style concerns voice and conventions while pedagogy concerns prerequisite knowledge and learning sequence.

conflict_rules: Accuracy, scope, and uncertainty outrank ease of explanation.
Exact source language is preserved in quoted or zero-drift zones and explained around rather than rewritten.
If audience level is materially ambiguous, provide a concise default plus an offer or branch for deeper detail.
strong_model_may_skip: printing an explicit audience profile for a familiar user
examples when the concept is already concrete

example.task_context: Explain an API breaking change to product managers.
example.why_activates: They need impact and rollout logic, not implementation-level type-system detail.
example.inputs_state: The technical migration guide, compatibility window, affected workflows, and rollback limitations are known.
example.does: Starts with user-visible impact, defines compatibility window in plain language, sequences rollout dependencies, and includes one workflow example while preserving rollback limits.
example.does_not: Replace the mechanism with a false everyday analogy or omit the irreversible deadline.
example.result: A technically faithful explanation that supports planning decisions.

distinctive_test.given: An accurate explanation assumes several prerequisites the target reader lacks.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill models the gap, orders prerequisites, defines terms, and back-checks simplifications.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill merely makes sentences shorter, changes tone, or removes technical limitations.

closest_neighbors.style-alignment: Adjusts voice and convention; Pedagogical Alignment adjusts conceptual path and prerequisite load.
closest_neighbors.explanation-minimality-scaffold: Deletes nonessential explanation; Pedagogical Alignment determines the essential bridge for this reader.

source_refs.heading: 17. VERBATIM-COPY / FIDELITY WORKFLOW — EXAMPLE OF UPGRADEABLE COMPOSITION

placeholder-suppression.summary: Blocks finalization until unfinished markers, dummy values, unresolved variables, and empty required sections are resolved, omitted, or clearly labeled.
placeholder-suppression.purpose: Prevent scaffolding artifacts from escaping as if they were complete content.
placeholder-suppression.problem_solved: Templates and multi-stage generation leave TODOs, bracket prompts, synthetic values, interpolation tokens, or structurally empty requirements that readers may mistake for finished output.
avoid_when: the deliverable is explicitly a template whose placeholders are the product
an example intentionally teaches placeholder syntax
redacted fields must retain an approved marker
placeholder-suppression.mechanism: Run a two-layer completion scan: a lexical detector for markers such as TODO, TBD, FIXME, bracket prompts, dummy domains, sample IDs, and unresolved interpolation syntax; then a schema detector for empty required sections, null required fields, and uninstantiated variables. Classify every hit using a narrow allowlist for intentional template, example, or redaction contexts; all other hits must be filled from authority, removed with requirement revalidation, or explicitly labeled unresolved before release.
procedure: Load the artifact's required sections, fields, and variable schema.
Scan text and code for known marker tokens, dummy values, bracketed instructions, and unresolved interpolation forms.
Scan structure for empty or default-valued required elements.
Classify hits as accidental, intentionally illustrative, approved redaction, or genuinely unresolved using context and an explicit allowlist.
Resolve accidental hits from authoritative inputs, omit only when the requirement permits, and label genuine gaps with impact and owner.
Rescan the final artifact and fail the release gate on any unclassified or accidental hit.
always_do: use contextual allowlisting rather than global token exceptions
distinguish explicit unresolved disclosure from accidental placeholder leakage
never_do: replace unknown values with plausible inventions
delete a required section just to clear the scan
flag every bracket in code or citation as a placeholder
allow an unclassified marker in final output

interaction_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite removes or labels placeholders without altering neighboring facts.
interaction_reasons.final-validation: Final Validation treats an unresolved accidental marker as a release-blocking defect.

counterbalance_reasons.template-preservation: An explicit template context protects intentional placeholders from destructive suppression.

redundancy_reasons.grounding-no-invention: Grounding prevents invented replacements; Placeholder Suppression specifically detects unfinished output artifacts and completion gaps.

conflict_rules: Never fabricate content to satisfy completion.
Approved template and example placeholders remain only when clearly scoped and non-executable.
A required unknown is labeled unresolved and blocks completion when the contract requires a concrete value.
strong_model_may_skip: reporting every zero-hit pattern in the final response

example.why_activates: README templates, manifests, and examples may retain setup prompts or dummy URLs.
example.inputs_state: Repository files, manifest schema, approved example fixtures, and project metadata are available.
example.does: Finds a `[your-org]` README token, an empty license field, and `example.com` in a test fixture; resolves the first two and allowlists the fixture by path before rescanning.
example.does_not: Replace the license with a guess or globally allow every `example.com` occurrence.
example.result: A release with no accidental placeholders and one documented intentional fixture.

distinctive_test.given: A final artifact contains TODO text, one empty required field, and a placeholder intentionally shown in an example.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill catches lexical and structural defects, resolves or blocks them, and narrowly allowlists the instructional example.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill only searches for TODO, deletes unknowns, invents values, or suppresses the intentional example.

closest_neighbors.grounding-no-invention: Stops fabricated content; Placeholder Suppression finds and classifies unfinished markers and empty requirements.
closest_neighbors.safe-rewrite: Performs meaning-preserving wording changes; Placeholder Suppression owns the completion gate.

placeholder-suppression.notes: The source explicitly recovers representative marker classes and the resolve, omit, or explicitly label rule before final output.

source_refs.heading: 8. Tier-3 / Paper-Author alignment family recovered from late-November work

style-alignment.summary: Conforms output to an authorized voice and presentation contract without changing facts, reasoning, evidence status, or task compliance.
style-alignment.purpose: Make artifacts consistent with audience, publication, or organizational style while keeping truth and requirements dominant.
style-alignment.problem_solved: Style can be inconsistent or inappropriate, but style imitation and polishing can also distort claims, citations, uncertainty, or required structure.
avoid_when: the requested style impersonates a living person or conflicts with policy
exact quoted language must remain untouched
facts or reasoning are not yet stable
style-alignment.mechanism: Translate the authorized style request into an observable style vector—tone, formality, sentence rhythm, vocabulary level, structure, formatting, and disallowed tendencies—while extracting a separate semantic invariant ledger. Transform surface choices toward the style vector, protect quoted and zero-drift zones, then score both conformance and semantic preservation; truth, task, and citation constraints veto any stylistic gain.
procedure: Extract the authorized style source and convert it into observable positive and negative constraints.
Lock facts, reasoning relations, requirements, citations, uncertainty, and exact-text zones.
Revise diction, rhythm, organization, and formatting only where the style contract permits.
Compare the result against the style vector using representative passages rather than vague resemblance.
Run a semantic and citation diff; revert any stylistic change that alters truth, logic, or attribution.
always_do: keep style subordinate to truth and task
never_do: invent facts or confidence to sound more authoritative
mimic unauthorized personal quirks
let brand voice erase required warnings
treat subjective vibe as the only acceptance test

interaction_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite provides the semantic invariant checks during style transformation.
interaction_reasons.pedagogical-alignment: Pedagogical Alignment adjusts conceptual accessibility independently of voice.
interaction_reasons.citation-fidelity: Citation Fidelity ensures moved or rewritten claims remain correctly supported.

counterbalance_reasons.grounding-no-invention: Grounding vetoes stylish additions that lack source support.
counterbalance_reasons.explanation-minimality-scaffold: Minimality prevents style requirements from producing ornamental excess.

redundancy_reasons.safe-rewrite: Safe Rewrite governs preservation across any rewrite; Style Alignment supplies the specific target dimensions and conformance check.
redundancy_reasons.pedagogical-alignment: Both adapt to users, but style changes voice and form while pedagogy changes conceptual scaffolding.

conflict_rules: Truth, safety, citation fidelity, and explicit task constraints outrank the style guide.
Exact quotations and legally controlled text are excluded from stylistic transformation.
When two style authorities conflict, use the source explicitly designated for this artifact or ask rather than blend them silently.
strong_model_may_skip: publishing the full style vector for a short answer
scoring every sentence independently

example.task_context: Convert contributions from several authors into one neutral technical guide.
example.why_activates: Voice and formatting vary while facts and citations are already approved.
example.inputs_state: A house guide specifies concise neutral prose, heading conventions, and prohibited marketing language.
example.does: Builds a style vector, normalizes voice and headings, removes promotional phrasing, and confirms claims, uncertainty, and citations remain unchanged.
example.does_not: Add confident benefit claims to make the guide sound polished.
example.result: A consistent guide that retains the approved semantic record.

distinctive_test.given: A factual draft must match a defined house style.
distinctive_test.expect: The skill extracts observable style dimensions, transforms only surface form, protects exact zones, and validates facts and citations.
distinctive_test.reject: The skill claims generic polish, alters reasoning for voice, or judges success only by subjective resemblance.

closest_neighbors.safe-rewrite: Protects semantics for any rewrite; Style Alignment additionally defines and tests a target voice.
closest_neighbors.pedagogical-alignment: Optimizes conceptual accessibility; Style Alignment optimizes voice and presentation convention.
closest_neighbors.explanation-minimality-scaffold: Controls content quantity; Style Alignment controls presentation of retained content.

style-alignment.notes: The recovered source makes style explicitly subordinate to truth and task requirements; the style-vector representation is a concrete normalization of that constraint.
